questions.stem: Sound waves are LONGITUDINAL mechanical waves and need a medium to propagate. The speed of sound in AIR at 20°C is approximately:
questions.explanation: SPEED OF SOUND in AIR: ~343 m/s at 20°C (~1235 km/h). Increases with temperature (~0.6 m/s per °C rise). Formula: v = 331 + 0.6 × T (T in °C). SPEED OF SOUND in DIFFERENT MEDIA: AIR ~343 m/s; WATER ~1480 m/s (~4.3× air); STEEL ~5960 m/s (~17× air); DIAMOND ~12000 m/s. General rule: faster in SOLIDS than LIQUIDS than GASES (because molecules are closer in solids, transmitting vibrations faster). VACUUM — SOUND CANNOT travel (no medium). SPEED OF LIGHT in vacuum: c = 3 × 10⁸ m/s — ~874,000× faster than sound in air. This is why thunder FOLLOWS lightning (flash first, bang later — 3s per km). SONIC BOOM: aircraft exceeding sound speed (Mach 1, 1235 km/h sea level). MACH NUMBER = ratio of object speed to speed of sound (Mach 1, 2, 3...). HYPERSONIC: Mach 5+. Concorde flew Mach 2.04. First supersonic flight: Chuck Yeager 14 Oct 1947 (Bell X-1).

questions.stem: The AUDIBLE range of sound for HUMANS is:
questions.explanation: HUMAN AUDIBLE RANGE: 20 Hz to 20 kHz. Below 20 Hz = INFRASOUND (elephants, whales communicate here; earthquakes generate these; also caused by volcanic eruptions, thunder, wind turbines). Above 20 kHz = ULTRASOUND (used in MEDICAL IMAGING — sonography; SONAR; cleaning; industrial testing). With age, high-frequency hearing degrades (presbycusis) — many adults lose hearing above 15-16 kHz. OTHER ANIMAL HEARING RANGES: Dogs: 67 Hz - 45 kHz (why dog whistles work — ultrasonic for humans). Cats: 55 Hz - 79 kHz. Bats: 2 kHz - 110 kHz (use echolocation up to 200 kHz!). Dolphins: 150 Hz - 150 kHz. Mice: 1 kHz - 90 kHz. Elephants: 16 Hz - 12 kHz (strong infrasonic communication, can hear distant storms). Frequencies: HIGHER FREQ = HIGHER PITCH. AMPLITUDE = volume (measured in decibels, dB). Piano middle C = 261.6 Hz. Wavelength × frequency = speed.

questions.stem: The DOPPLER EFFECT — apparent change in frequency of a wave as the source or observer moves — was first formulated by:
questions.explanation: DOPPLER EFFECT: proposed by Christian Andreas DOPPLER (Austrian physicist, 1842). Observed frequency > emitted when source approaches observer; < when moving away. Everyday example: AMBULANCE siren — sounds higher pitch as it approaches, lower as it recedes. Formula (non-relativistic): f_observed = f_source × (v ± v_observer) / (v ± v_source), where v = speed of wave in medium. APPLICATIONS: (1) DOPPLER RADAR — police speed guns; weather radar (measures wind speed); (2) RED SHIFT in astronomy — light from distant galaxies shifts to red (longer wavelength) = receding; Edwin Hubble's 1929 work showed galaxies receding proportional to distance → Universe is expanding → Big Bang evidence. (3) MEDICAL DOPPLER — blood flow velocity via ultrasound. (4) SONAR, bat echolocation, air traffic control. RELATIVISTIC DOPPLER EFFECT: Einstein's generalisation accounting for time dilation. Doppler predicted applicability to light — proven experimentally only 3 years later.

questions.stem: The ELECTROMAGNETIC SPECTRUM (in order of INCREASING frequency / DECREASING wavelength) is:

options.option_text: Radio → Microwaves → Infrared → Visible light → UV → X-rays → Gamma rays
Gamma → X-rays → UV → Visible → Infrared → Microwaves → Radio

questions.explanation: EM SPECTRUM (low to high frequency): RADIO WAVES (long wavelength, low frequency, low energy; AM/FM radio, TV, WiFi) → MICROWAVES (ovens, cell phones, radar, satellite comms) → INFRARED (heat, remote controls, thermography) → VISIBLE LIGHT (tiny slice humans see: red→orange→yellow→green→blue→indigo→violet = VIBGYOR in reverse) → ULTRAVIOLET (sunburn, vitamin D, sterilisation) → X-RAYS (medical imaging, airport scanners) → GAMMA RAYS (shortest wavelength, highest energy; nuclear reactions, cosmic rays — very penetrating). ALL travel at SPEED OF LIGHT in vacuum (c = 3 × 10⁸ m/s). c = λf (wavelength × frequency). Visible light: 400-700 nm wavelength; 430-770 THz. Discovered by MAXWELL (theoretical predictions, 1865), HEINRICH HERTZ (radio waves, 1887), W.C. RÖNTGEN (X-rays, 1895, Nobel 1901 first-ever). Photons carry energy E = hf = hc/λ (h = Planck's constant). EM waves don't need a medium (can travel in vacuum, unlike sound).

questions.stem: ECHOES are produced when sound reflects off a surface. For the reflected sound to be perceived as a distinct echo (not just reverberation), the reflecting surface must be AT LEAST how far away from the source?

options.option_text: ~17 metres (so total travel time ≥ 0.1 seconds, the human ear's resolution)

questions.explanation: ECHO REQUIREMENT: the reflected sound must reach the listener's ear at LEAST 0.1 seconds AFTER the original sound (persistence of hearing / auditory resolution). Time = distance/speed → in air (v=343 m/s): 0.1 s means round trip ≥ 34 m → reflector must be ≥ 17 m away. Below that distance, sound blurs into REVERBERATION. Examples: WHISPERING GALLERIES (St. Paul's Cathedral London, Gol Gumbaz Bijapur, US Capitol) — sound travels along curved walls. SONAR (SOund Navigation And Ranging): uses ultrasonic waves + echo timing to measure ocean depth or locate objects underwater. BAT ECHOLOCATION: emit 50-200 kHz pulses, listen for echoes. RADAR (RAdio Detection And Ranging): EM waves + echo for aircraft/weather tracking. ULTRASOUND IMAGING: uses ~1-20 MHz ultrasound + echo to image internal body organs (prenatal, cardiac). Reverberation: useful in concert halls (designed for ~1.5-2s reverberation time); but poor in classrooms or homes where clarity is needed.

questions.stem: Sound INTENSITY is measured on a LOGARITHMIC scale called:
questions.explanation: DECIBEL (dB) = log-scale unit for sound intensity. Named after Alexander Graham BELL (inventor of the phone; B = bel; dB = decibel, 1/10th). Formula: dB = 10 × log₁₀(I/I₀), where I₀ = reference = 10⁻¹² W/m² (threshold of human hearing). Every 10 dB = 10× intensity. 20 dB = 100× intensity. COMMON SOUND LEVELS: 0 dB — threshold of hearing; 10 dB — breathing; 20-30 dB — whisper; 40 dB — library; 60 dB — normal conversation; 70 dB — vacuum cleaner; 80-90 dB — city traffic; 90-100 dB — subway, motorcycle; 100 dB — chainsaw; 110 dB — rock concert, baby crying close; 120 dB — jet takeoff at 60 m; 130 dB — threshold of PAIN; 140 dB — jet engine at 30 m; >140 dB — immediate hearing damage. NOISE POLLUTION in India regulated by Noise Pollution (Regulation and Control) Rules 2000 — day/night limits in industrial/commercial/residential/silence zones. Noise-induced hearing loss (NIHL) is permanent above 85 dB sustained exposure.

questions.stem: When light passes from a LESS DENSE medium (air) to a MORE DENSE medium (water or glass), it:

options.option_text: Speeds up and bends AWAY from the normal
Slows down and bends TOWARDS the normal
Continues in a straight line with no change

questions.explanation: REFRACTION of LIGHT: when a light ray passes from one medium to another with different optical density, it CHANGES DIRECTION (bends) at the interface AND changes speed. From LESS DENSE (e.g., air) to MORE DENSE (e.g., water/glass): light SLOWS DOWN and bends TOWARDS the normal (the perpendicular to the surface). Vice versa: from dense to less dense, light SPEEDS UP and bends AWAY from the normal. SNELL'S LAW: n₁ sin θ₁ = n₂ sin θ₂, where n = refractive index (n_vacuum = 1, n_air ≈ 1.0003, n_water ≈ 1.33, n_glass ≈ 1.5, n_diamond ≈ 2.42). SPEED OF LIGHT in a medium: v = c/n. TOTAL INTERNAL REFLECTION (TIR): when light tries to move from dense to less dense medium at an angle > CRITICAL ANGLE, ALL light reflects back. Applications: OPTICAL FIBRES (internet cables), MIRAGE (hot air acts as less dense; road appears wet), SPARKLE OF DIAMOND (high n + cutting causes TIR from many facets). Critical angle for water-air: ~48.6°; glass-air: ~42°; diamond-air: ~24.4°.

questions.stem: A RAINBOW is formed by THREE optical phenomena acting on sunlight interacting with water droplets. These are:

options.option_text: Refraction, total internal reflection, and dispersion

questions.explanation: RAINBOW formation: (1) SUNLIGHT enters water droplet — REFRACTION at entry surface (white light bends into droplet); (2) hits back wall of droplet — TOTAL INTERNAL REFLECTION (if within critical angle limits); (3) exits droplet — another REFRACTION. Throughout, DISPERSION (different wavelengths bend by slightly different amounts — because refractive index depends on wavelength) separates white light into COLOURS: VIBGYOR (Violet, Indigo, Blue, Green, Yellow, Orange, Red). RED on OUTER edge (least bent, ~42° from sun-anti point); VIOLET on INNER (most bent, ~40°). OBSERVER is between sun and raindrops — must have sun BEHIND + rain in front; rainbow appears in an arc centred on the anti-solar point. DOUBLE RAINBOW: faint outer rainbow with REVERSED colours, formed by 2 internal reflections (~51°-54°). Alexander's dark band between them (no light bounces into it). Colours are continuous, not discrete 7 — we see 7 by convention (Newton's division). No two people see the SAME rainbow — position-dependent optical illusion.
